title: The major scale across the neck
description: Map C major string by string, treat boxes as windows, and rebuild any key from pitch classes.

cards.front: What is a major scale on guitar, if not a shape?
cards.back: Seven pitch classes repeated everywhere they occur. Spell the scale, find every occurrence of each class on each string, then choose a region and play the notes found there.

cards.front: Why should construction come before boxes?
cards.back: Shapes and boxes are the result of choosing a region, not the starting point. Learn shapes first and you can play but cannot say what you are playing. Learn construction first and the shapes appear on their own in any key.

cards.front: What is standard tuning string to string, and where does the pattern shift?
cards.back: E A D G B E. Adjacent opens are a P4 (5 frets) except strings 3–2 (G→B), a M3 (4 frets). Any pattern that crosses 3–2 shifts by one fret, which is why shapes look different on different string pairs.

cards.front: On any single string, where do major-scale notes sit relative to a root fret?
cards.back: Fret offsets 0 2 4 5 7 9 11 12. Each note then appears in a different place on every string because each string starts at a different pitch.

cards.front: Why does a four-fret window always catch at least two scale notes per string?
cards.back: The scale has no gap larger than a whole step. Three notes versus two depends on where the half steps (3–4 and 7–8) fall in that window.

cards.front: Map C major on strings 6 and 1 in frets 0–12 (note:fret).
cards.back: Both are E strings, so they match: E:0 F:1 G:3 A:5 B:7 C:8 D:10 E:12.

cards.front: Map C major on string 5 in frets 0–12 (note:fret).
Map C major on string 4 in frets 0–12 (note:fret).
Map C major on string 3 in frets 0–12 (note:fret).
Map C major on string 2 in frets 0–12 (note:fret).
Which C major notes fall in frets 7–10, string by string?
cards.back: 6: B:7 C:8 D:10. 5: E:7 F:8 G:10. 4: A:7 B:9 C:10. 3: D:7 E:9 F:10. 2: G:8 A:10. 1: B:7 C:8 D:10. Three notes on most strings, two on string 2 because of the G-to-B gap.

cards.front: In the frets 7–10 window of C major, where are the roots, and which degrees does the window contain?
cards.back: Roots at string 6 fret 8, string 4 fret 10, and string 1 fret 8. The window contains every degree at least once. String 6 fret 8 is degree 1; string 5 fret 10 is degree 5.

cards.front: Play one octave of C major across strings 6, 5, and 4.
cards.back: String 6: C:8 D:10. String 5: E:7 F:8 G:10. String 4: A:7 B:9 C:10. Two notes, then three, then three — same scale, different grouping.

cards.front: G major vs C major on strings 4 and 3: what is the only change, and which frets move?
cards.back: Only F becomes F♯. String 4: F:3 becomes F♯:4. String 3: F:10 becomes F♯:11. Moving key changes the window, not the method.

cards.front: Write D major and place it on string 4 from the open string.
cards.back: D E F♯ G A B C♯ D at frets 0 2 4 5 7 9 11 12.

cards.front: Build G major on string 3 from the open string.
cards.back: G A B C D E F♯ G at frets 0 2 4 5 7 9 11 12.

cards.front: Place A major on string 5 from the open string, then on string 6 from fret 5.
cards.back: String 5 frets 0 2 4 5 7 9 11 12. String 6 frets 5 7 9 10 12 14 16 17. Notes: A B C♯ D E F♯ G♯ (A).

cards.front: From the C major map, list the scale notes in frets 2–5, string by string.
Play one octave of C major on string 3 and on string 2. What frets?
cards.back: String 3: 5 7 9 10 12 14 16 17. String 2: 1 3 5 6 8 10 12 13. Same sound; frets differ because the strings start on different pitches.

cards.front: Build F major on string 6 from fret 1. Frets and notes?
cards.back: Frets 1 3 5 6 8 10 12 13 give F G A B♭ C D E F.

cards.front: The first phrase of “Happy Birthday” is degrees 5 5 6 5 8 7. What notes is that in C major?
cards.back: G G A G C B. Play it in two different regions of the neck.
